sentences.text: Juncitarsus is currently classified as a basal member of the Mirandornithes clade, a group that includes flamingos but does not contain true flamingos.
Fossil remains include at least three adults or near-adults alongside one chick that could not fly when it died.
Evidence suggests this wading bird lived in colonies.

Fossils were collected in 1946 and 1947 in the Bridger Formation of Wyoming by Charles Lewis Gazin, Franklin L. Pearce, and George F. Sternberg before the genus was formally named in 1980 by Storrs L. Olson and Alan Feduccia.
A second species, J. merkeli, was named in 1987 by Stefan Peters based on fossils from Germany.
The wading lifestyle of Juncitarsus is considered a derived feature that evolved independently from its swimming waterbird ancestors.
Juncitarsus lived during the Eocene epoch in the United States and Germany, specifically between 51.1 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
Researchers originally debated whether Juncitarsus was the earliest flamingo or related to avocets and stilts due to similarities with Recurvirostridae.
